4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The final preparations for Sordland's new Constitution were nearly complete. Soon, it would be presented in the Grand National Assembly; after that, it would be up to the Supreme Court to approve the changes. Including the ones that diminished the Justices' own power.

11.speaker: Player
11.text: "I've been looking forward to speaking with you in private, Mr. Kibener."

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: We had strong support in the party and the Assembly, but I wanted a landslide victory in order to force a yes out of the Court. So I had invited Kesaro Kibener, leader of the National Front Party, to have a private chat about my proposal. He was supposed to be in my office 20 minutes ago.

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: The final preparations for Sordland's new Constitution were nearly complete. Soon, it would be presented in the Grand National Assembly; a huge step for our administration. Then it would be on to the Supreme Court.

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: I was halfway through my second coffee of the day when Kibener finally entered. He was wearing a brown suit with his party's pin neatly attached. After firmly shaking hands, he sat down.

17.speaker: Narrator
17.text: I knew I was on shaky ground with the Assembly. I desperately needed more votes. So I had invited Kesaro Kibener, leader of the National Front Party, to have a private chat about my proposal. He was supposed to be in my office 20 minutes ago.

19.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
19.text: "Likewise, President Rayne. We have much to discuss."

20.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
20.text: "I was stopped by the police on my way here. I seem to be subject to more and more such 'random' checks these days."

21.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
21.text: "I hope you don't mind the slight delay. I was stopped by the police on my way here. I seem to be subject to more and more such 'random' checks these days."

22.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
22.text: "Some key figures in my party are also reporting obstructions from the state. It seems that your reforms aren't sitting well with certain members of the Old Guard."

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: He pulled out a cigarette along with a Rippo lighter and lit it up.

24.speaker: Player
24.text: "You didn't even ask me if you could smoke in my office."

25.speaker: Player
25.text: "Have you forgotten common courtesy, Mr. Kibener? Are we not offering cigarettes to friends anymore?"

27.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
27.text: "Apologies. May I smoke in your office, Mr. President?"

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: Our eyes locked. After trying to stare me down for a few moments, Kesaro finally gave in and extinguished his cigarette.

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: He passed a cigarette to me and lit it up.

35.speaker: Narrator
35.text: I took a look at his lighter as he put it down on the table. It was a regular Rippo, but the shape appeared to be malformed.

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: Looking more closely, I could see a large circular dent in the chrome plating.

38.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
38.text: "Believe it or not, this lighter is the reason I'm alive today. I should be thankful that the damn assassin was Bludish. No wonder he was incompetent."

39.speaker: Narrator
39.text: He pulled on his collar to reveal the scar on his neck.

40.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
40.text: "Maybe I'll tell you the full story some other time. For now, let's talk about our collaboration. I know why you called me here."

41.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
41.text: "But before we get into the proposal, I'd like to discuss a few topics that I believe to be of higher priority."

42.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
42.text: "The lighter took the first shot. The second one grazed me right here."

43.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
43.text: "I may not be fond of President Smolak, but our joint operation with the Wehzeks was certainly successful in stamping out the BFF. I consider that a great success."

44.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
44.text: "The Bludish independence movement, for example. Not only do the separatists pose an existential risk to us, they also threaten our neighbors in Wehlen."

48.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
48.text: "That brings me to the Religious Harmony Bill."

49.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
49.text: "Now, Rumburg will have a harder time trying to influence us from within. Let's not forget their caches of KA-74s in our country. You've done the right thing."

50.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
50.text: "That's right. They don't even know whom they are dealing with."

51.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
51.text: "Closing the borders with Wehlen has helped, but the countryside of Nargis and Bergia continues to be plagued by the BFF."

52.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
52.text: "Wehlen continues to be plagued by the BFF. They use their secret bases in the mountains to launch infiltrations into Sordland."

58.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
58.text: "They are a weaker nation both in heart and might. They won't have the capacity to handle the Bludish threat."

59.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
59.text: "Rumburg is using them to weaken us, and they might succeed if we do nothing to stop them. Let's not forget their caches of KA-74s in our country."

60.speaker: Player
60.text: "The support President Smolak received from United Contana was a concern, but realpolitik was the victor."

61.speaker: Player
61.text: "Rumburg and the BFF will both meet a bad end if they dare to divide Sordland."

62.speaker: Player
62.text: "We can't intervene in other countries. It would destabilize the region."

63.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
63.text: "A Sordish president has to do whatever is necessary to protect his people."

64.speaker: Player
64.text: "Wehlen could be a valuable ally in the future, now that we have established a closer relationship."

65.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
65.text: "Rumburg is using them to weaken us. Hopefully, our increased military funding will make sure their efforts won't bear fruit. But we need to stay vigilant. Let's not forget their caches of KA-74s in our country."

66.speaker: Player
66.text: "Wehlen can take care of their own problems, and we will take care of ours."

74.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
74.text: "Thanks to your support, the BFF and other extremist groups won't be able to use religion to organise and gain support among the common folk."

78.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
78.text: "But you decided to veto it. Why are you ignoring the problem? The Bludish are using Nurity as a tool in their quest for independence. This is a direct threat."

79.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
79.text: "If anything, we are not restrictive enough. But I will not dive into this further."

80.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
80.text: "In this case, doing nothing is far worse. The BFF is actively using priests in majority-Bludish areas. But let's not get off track."

81.speaker: Player
81.text: "The bill was practically a recruitment flyer for the BFF. The more of these we pass, the more followers they get."

82.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
82.text: "Thank you. I led the effort. I was happy but not surprised to receive so much support from my fellow MPs."

83.speaker: Player
83.text: "It was too restrictive on the Bludish people. I couldn't let it pass."

84.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
84.text: "In an ideal world, yes. But as long as the BFF exists, that is not the world we live in."

85.speaker: Player
85.text: "We need to find a way where we can coexist without violence."

86.speaker: Player
86.text: "The Bludish problem must be solved. We can't have an independence movement inside Sordland."

87.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
87.text: "I'm glad you and I agree on this issue."

88.speaker: Player
88.text: "It was a well-written and strong bill. It would have been wrong to veto it."

89.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
89.text: "Our party and many members of parliament worked extremely hard on the proposal."

90.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
90.text: "Look. I went over your proposed constitutional changes..."

102.text: "You do realize the NFP's current share of the vote is under this threshold, don't you? You're attempting to get my party to participate in its own destruction."

103.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
103.text: "You know that I will fight this until my last breath if I have to."

104.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
104.text: "So I am asking you now. What did you even call me here for?"

105.speaker: Player
105.text: "To find a middle ground. Scratch my back and I will scratch yours."

106.speaker: Player
106.text: "I need you to help me, Kesaro. With your support, we can do a lot of good for Sordland."

108.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
108.text: "If you want me to even consider supporting you, you will change the draft and you will change it now."

110.speaker: Player
110.text: "I will not change anything in the draft. I have already decided on these points."

111.speaker: Player
111.text: "Fine. I will change the election threshold in return for your support."

112.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
112.text: "You will keep the election threshold where it has always been, at 10%."

113.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
113.text: "Then there is no point in continuing this conversation, is there?"

114.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
114.text: "Before I go, I guarantee you this. That proposal will not pass the Assembly. I will make sure of it."

115.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
115.text: "Good luck, Mr. President. You're bound to need it."

116.speaker: Player
116.text: "Very well. You will get what you want. The election threshold will remain the same."

117.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
117.text: "Anything other than that, and you can kiss our support goodbye. In fact, the NFP will fight very hard to prevent this bill from passing."

118.speaker: Player
118.text: "Then try your best to fight the bill, Kesaro. You won't get far."

119.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
119.text: "If you only knew how many times I've heard that. Yet look where I am."

121.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
121.text: "Very good. Now we are getting somewhere."

123.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
123.text: "Don't you understand what will happen when you decrease the threshold? Our Assembly will be overrun with Bludish and communist traitors."

343.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
343.text: "Then there is no use in continuing this conversation, is there?"

344.speaker: Narrator
344.text: Kesaro stood up and looked down at me.

345.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
345.text: "They can speak to each other in whatever language they want. But they must learn Sordish. That's it."

346.speaker: Player
346.text: "If they live in Sordland, they need to know how to speak in Sordish."

347.speaker: Player
347.text: "You will get your signature. I will sign the bill when I receive it."

348.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
348.text: "Before I go, I guarantee you this. That bill will not pass the Assembly. I will make sure of it."

349.speaker: Player
349.text: "So your answer is to ban them completely from speaking Bludish at school?"

350.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
350.text: "This bill, I call it the Unified Education Language Act, will enforce our language as the only one accepted in educational institutions."

351.speaker: Player
351.text: "I will decide when I see the bill. Not before."

352.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
352.text: "I went to the nearby villages. All of them were the same! Not a single soul spoke Sordish! That put me on the path to draft a new bill."

355.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
355.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_A_Kesaro_Ban_RY"] == true  or  (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanBoth"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_A_Kesaro_RevertBan_YS"] == true)  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanRedYouth"] == true

356.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
356.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_A_Kesaro_Ban_RY"] == true  or  (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanBoth"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_A_Kesaro_RevertBan_YS"] == true)  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanRedYouth"] == true) == false

357.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
357.text: "Will you do the right thing for Sordland? What do you think?"
357.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_A_Kesaro_Ban_RY"] == true  or  (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanBoth"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn06_A_Kesaro_RevertBan_YS"] == true)  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn03_StabilityOrder_BanRedYouth"] == true

358.speaker: Player
358.text: "You will get your signature. I will sign the bill when I receive it."

359.speaker: Player
359.text: "I don't think so. I won't go along with your scheme."

362.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
362.text: "But regardless, I think we have achieved much today."

363.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
363.text: "Here is what I had in mind."

364.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
364.text: "Very well. The NFP and I will support you in your reform package."

370.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
370.text: "One last thing before we shake hands."

371.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
371.text: "I see your willingness to cooperate with me and I applaud it."

372.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
372.text: "What do you think about taking things a step further?"

373.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
373.text: "An alliance between our two parties. We would be extremely powerful in the Assembly."

374.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
374.text: "It would open many doors for both of us."

375.speaker: Player
375.text: "Apologies, but I have to refuse. It would close more doors than it would open."

376.speaker: Player
376.text: "I'm glad you asked. How better to cement our newfound partnership than with an alliance?"

379.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
379.text: "It will be tough to convince our respective parties, but I believe the good we'll do for Sordland together will be worth the hurdle."

380.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
380.text: "I understand. Just keep it in mind."

381.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
381.text: "Well then, Mr. President. My respect for you has increased a hundredfold within the short span of this meeting."

385.speaker: Player
385.text: "Make sure you deliver your end of the promise."

386.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
386.text: "I have never broken my word in my life."

388.speaker: Narrator
388.text: We shook hands and Kesaro turned around to leave.

389.speaker: Narrator
389.text: Kesaro closed the door and left my office.

390.speaker: Narrator
390.text: He closed the door and left my office.

434.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
434.text: "I also wanted to talk about the aid you received from United Contana."

435.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
435.text: "Do you think that's just free money? Do you think they offered it out of sheer goodwill?"

436.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
436.text: "You were fooled. They saw Sordland battling the recession and they pounced on it."

437.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
437.text: "You sold our national pride for money."

438.speaker: Player
438.text: "It was a necessary evil. Don't expect me to sit by while my people suffer."

439.speaker: Player
439.text: "I don't see anything wrong with accepting a helping hand."

440.speaker: Player
440.text: "Is your national pride so fragile that this will destroy it? I don't think so."

441.speaker: Player
441.text: "Kesaro. I am the President. I won't allow you to talk to me like this."

442.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
442.text: "Of course. My apologies. I'll get to the point."

443.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
443.text: "I fought for my country many times, and I have the scars to prove it. Can you say the same?"

445.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
445.text: "I won't waste my breath further on this matter, since you clearly don't understand."

453.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
453.text: "In the end, it's only a 2% difference."

456.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
456.text: "You bet, Mr. President. It's one of the firsts."

457.speaker: Narrator
457.text: He gave me the lighter. It was an original Rippo, but the shape appeared to be malformed.
